Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.160 of 2022 at Police Station-North, District-Firozabad under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 05.03.2022.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 27.02.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Ajay Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant did not torture the deceased or demand dowry.
3. The deceased was depressed as she was suffering from a chronic ailment which was not cured despite prolonged treatment.
4. On the fateful day, the deceased succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
5. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

6. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii).
The hyoid bone was intact.
7. The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
8. The prerequisite for attracting the presumption and the reversing the burden of proof are not established in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
9. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
10. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated in the investigation and has joined the trial proceedings.
The applicant never tampered with the evidence nor did he influence any witness.
11. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and and shows no sign of early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
12. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite detention of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
13. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
14. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-

In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Ravi @ Ravikant Verma be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
